moduleTitle: Adding optional Actions to a workflow
learningObjectives: Identify the role of optional Actions and optional Processes in a Case workflow.
Configure Case-wide and Stage-only optional Actions and explain how Promoted Actions behave at runtime.

elements.description: Two types of user-initiated additions to a Case workflow:
items: OPTIONAL USER ACTION — one Step users can invoke in its configured Case-wide or Stage-only scope.
OPTIONAL PROCESS — a series of Steps users can invoke in its configured scope.

elements.text: Think of an on-demand task menu: an agent can update a contact detail or launch cancellation when the task is applicable. Optional describes how the task is invoked, not a guarantee that its configured effect leaves the Case unchanged.

elements.description: Scope determines when the optional action is available:
items: CASE-WIDE — lifecycle scope rather than restriction to one Stage; availability still respects applicable configuration and user access.
STAGE-ONLY — offered in the configured Stage context, such as cancellation before shipping.

elements.description: At runtime, optional Actions are accessible from the Actions menu in the Case. Users choose whether to invoke them during Case processing.

The reviewed runtime selects a promoted user Action for a button on the Case summary panel: the first Stage-wide Action other than Edit details, or the first Case-wide Action if no Stage-wide Action is available. Optional Processes are not supported as promoted Actions; prominence does not grant access or execute the Action automatically.

elements.caption: Users invoke optional work when applicable. Its configured purpose can update data, change a Stage or cancel work; optional is not synonymous with no effect on the main lifecycle.

examPitfalls.title: Optional Action (single Step) vs. Optional Process (series of Steps)
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask which optional type to use when the user needs to perform a multi-step sub-workflow. Candidates select Optional Action for both. An Optional Action contains a single Step; an Optional Process contains a series of Steps — use the Process for multi-step optional sub-workflows.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Optional Action = single Step/View. Optional Process = series of Steps. When a multi-step optional workflow is needed (e.g., 'Cancel Order' with multiple Steps), use an optional Process.

examPitfalls.title: Stage-only Actions are only available in a specific Stage
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks how to restrict an Optional Action to be available only while the case is in a specific Stage. Candidates configure it as a standard Optional Action. Stage-only Optional Actions must be configured at the Stage level — they disappear from the Actions menu once the case leaves that Stage.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Case-wide = available at ANY point in the Case. Stage-only = available ONLY when the Case is in that specific Stage. Example: 'Cancel Order' is Stage-only in 'Confirm Billing Details' Stage.

examPitfalls.title: Optional Actions are user-initiated — not automatically triggered
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions describe a scenario and ask whether an Optional Action will run automatically when a condition is met. Candidates say yes. Optional Actions are always user-initiated — they appear in the Actions menu for the user to choose; they do not fire automatically based on conditions.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Optional Actions are always user-initiated. The user decides whether to invoke them from the Actions menu. They are NOT triggered automatically by the Case workflow.

examPitfalls.title: Promoted Actions appear as buttons on the Case Page — not just in the Actions menu
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The reviewed runtime promotes an eligible user Action to a Case summary button. Optional Processes are not supported; selecting Case-wide scope alone does not make every Action a button.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Review the source selection order and Action eligibility; promotion changes visibility rather than automatic execution or access.

examPitfalls.title: Configuration location: Workflow tab → Optional Actions (upper-right)
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask where Optional Actions are configured in App Studio. Candidates look in the Stages panel. Optional Actions are configured in the Workflow tab using the Optional Actions button in the upper-right area of the Case Life Cycle — not within a Stage's step list.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Open Optional Actions on the Workflow tab, then choose the relevant Case-wide or Stage-only configuration.

examPitfalls.title: Optional invocation does not imply no lifecycle effect
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Change Stage is a built-in optional Action, and cancellation can be an optional Process. Their invocation can change progression; do not guarantee that every optional task is nonblocking or never redirects work.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Separate optional availability from the behavior of the invoked task and test that behavior.

examPitfalls.title: Built-in optional Actions: 'Edit details' and 'Change Stage'
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The topic gives Edit details and Change Stage as built-in Case-wide examples. Do not extrapolate an exact universal count or unchangeable availability across all architectures and configurations.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Pega Platform includes built-in optional Actions like 'Edit details' and 'Change Stage'. These are Case-wide by default and appear in the Optional Actions tab alongside any custom ones you add.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A loan application allows a customer service agent to update the customer's contact information at any point during the application process. This is an optional, user-initiated single-step action. What should the SA configure?

options.text: An optional Action — a single Action users can invoke at any point during Case processing
An optional Process — a series of Steps users can invoke at any point during Case processing
A Change Stage Automation that redirects to an 'Update Contact' Stage when triggered
A conditional Process that runs whenever the Case reaches the contact update Stage

practiceQuiz.hint: Single Step, user-initiated, not required = optional Action.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A single optional user-initiated action uses an optional Action (not a Process). B is wrong because an optional Process is for multi-step workflows. C uses an automation, which is triggered automatically, not user-initiated. D describes a conditional Process in the required workflow, not an optional user-initiated action.

optionExplanations.A: A scoped single-Step user Action fits the requested on-demand contact update, without inserting a required lifecycle task.
optionExplanations.B: An optional Process represents a series of Steps; the stated one-screen task does not require that series.
optionExplanations.C: Stage redirection is not needed to represent this scoped single-Step update; it changes the lifecycle structure instead.
optionExplanations.D: A conditionally started required Process is a different invocation pattern from the agent choosing the update on demand.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An online shopping Case needs a user-invoked optional cancellation workflow with three distinct Steps: confirmation, refund and notification. Which optional-work type represents that series?

options.text: An optional Process — a series of Steps users can optionally invoke
An optional Action — a single Action covering all three Steps
An Alternate Stage named 'Cancel Order' that users can manually trigger
A When Condition that activates the cancellation Processes automatically

practiceQuiz.hint: A series of user-initiated optional Steps constitutes an optional Process, not an Action.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A series of optional Steps uses an optional Process. This is a choice within the optional-work types, not a denial that a separately designed cancellation lifecycle could use an Alternate Stage.

optionExplanations.A: The explicitly separate confirmation, refund and notification Steps fit the optional Process structure described by the source.
optionExplanations.B: The described single user Action does not itself represent the required series of separate workflow Steps.
optionExplanations.C: An Alternate Stage is a different lifecycle design; this question asks for the optional-work type representing the series.
optionExplanations.D: An automatically evaluated condition does not provide the requested user invocation of this optional workflow.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'Cancel Order' optional Process should only be available when the Case is in the 'Confirm Billing Details' Stage. What scope should the SA configure?

options.text: Stage-only — available only when the Case is in that specific Stage
Case-wide — available throughout the entire Case lifecycle
Process-scoped — linked to a specific Process within the Stage
User-scoped — available only to users with the Manager Persona

practiceQuiz.hint: Available only in a specific Stage = Stage-only.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Stage-only is the source’s scope for work applicable in one Stage. User permissions are a separate concern from this lifecycle scope; the question does not define all possible access controls.

optionExplanations.A: Stage-only is the direct scope for the task that is relevant only during Confirm Billing Details.
optionExplanations.B: Case-wide is broader lifecycle scope and does not express the requested Stage-only availability directly.
optionExplanations.C: Process-scoped is not one of the two optional-work scope choices described by the source topic.
optionExplanations.D: A user permission restriction addresses who can act, not the specified Stage-only lifecycle availability.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An 'Update Contact' optional Action should be available at any point during the loan application — not restricted to a specific Stage. What scope is correct?

options.text: Case-wide — available throughout the entire Case lifecycle
Stage-only — configured on every Stage individually
Global — available across all Case Types in the application
Assignment-scoped — available only during the Assignment where it is configured

practiceQuiz.hint: Available at any point throughout the Case = Case-wide.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Case-wide provides lifecycle-wide scope without duplicating the Action across Stages. It does not automatically share the Action across every Case Type or override applicability and permissions.

optionExplanations.A: Case-wide avoids restricting this task to one Stage; configuration and access still determine actual availability.
optionExplanations.B: Repeating Stage configuration is not the direct lifecycle-wide scope requested, even if another design could duplicate availability.
optionExplanations.C: Case-wide means this Case’s lifecycle scope, not global exposure across all Case Types in the application.
optionExplanations.D: An Assignment-specific association is a different interaction context from lifecycle-wide optional availability.

practiceQuiz.scenario: At runtime, a user needs to invoke an optional Action to update their address during Case processing. Where do they find available optional Actions?

options.text: The Actions menu in the Case
The Case Life Cycle Workflow tab — they click 'Optional Actions' in the upper-right
The Stage header — a dropdown appears on the current Stage
The Assignment form — optional Actions appear as extra tabs on the current Assignment

practiceQuiz.hint: Runtime access to optional Actions is through the Actions menu.
practiceQuiz.rationale: At runtime, optional Actions are accessible from the Actions menu in the Case. B is the design-time configuration location — not the runtime access point. C and D are incorrect runtime locations.

optionExplanations.A: The source’s runtime Actions menu exposes applicable optional work; promoted buttons are an additional eligible-user-Action presentation.
optionExplanations.B: The Workflow tab is an authoring location for configuring optional work, not the requested runtime invocation menu.
optionExplanations.C: The topic identifies the Case Actions menu, not a universal current-Stage header dropdown, for this runtime access.
optionExplanations.D: Assignment tabs are not the runtime access route described in this source; optional work is offered through Actions.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the reviewed runtime, an eligible user Action is selected for a button on the Case summary panel rather than being accessed only through the Actions menu. What is this behavior called?

options.text: Promoted Actions — elevates the optional Action to appear as a button on the Case Page
Pinned Actions — pins the Action to the top of the Actions menu
Configure the optional Action as Case-wide — Case-wide Actions automatically appear as buttons
Set the Action priority to 'High' in the Optional Actions configuration

practiceQuiz.hint: A specific feature promotes optional Actions to the Case Page as visible buttons.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The source calls this a promoted Action. Runtime selection and eligible user-Action type matter; Case-wide scope or a supposed priority flag alone is not the described selection mechanism.

optionExplanations.A: Promoted Action names the described summary-button behavior; eligibility and runtime selection still determine which task appears.
optionExplanations.B: Pinned Actions is not the name given by this source to the selected summary-button behavior.
optionExplanations.C: Case-wide scope alone does not automatically select every Action for promotion; the source states a runtime selection behavior.
optionExplanations.D: A supposed High priority value is not the promotion selection procedure described in the source topic.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Can the optional multi-step Cancel Order Process be a promoted Action button under the reviewed runtime’s supported types?

options.text: No — the reviewed promotion behavior supports user Actions, not optional Processes
Yes — every optional Process is automatically promoted
Yes — only Processes, never user Actions, can be promoted
Yes — making it Stage-only automatically removes the type restriction

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish an optional Process from an eligible promoted user Action.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The source supports only user Actions as promoted Actions. Optional Processes retain their optional-work role but cannot be promoted through this behavior; changing scope does not change their type.

optionExplanations.A: The reviewed type restriction permits user Actions and excludes optional Processes, regardless of the Process’s scope.
optionExplanations.B: Optional Processes are explicitly excluded from promotion by this source, so universal automatic promotion is incorrect.
optionExplanations.C: This reverses the source distinction: user Actions are supported, while optional Processes are excluded.
optionExplanations.D: Stage-only scope does not convert a multi-Step Process into the eligible user-Action type for promotion.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where in App Studio does an SA configure optional Actions for a Case Type?

options.text: Workflow tab → click 'Optional Actions' in the upper-right corner of the Case Life Cycle
Stage properties panel → 'Optional' section for each Stage
A separate 'Optional Actions' form under Case Type settings
Users > User Management in App Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: Optional Actions are configured from the Workflow tab's upper-right corner.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The source opens Optional Actions from the Workflow tab and offers Case-wide and Stage-only work there. This is the documented procedure, not a universal claim about all authoring routes.

optionExplanations.A: This is the documented entry point that displays and adds both Case-wide and Stage-only optional work.
optionExplanations.B: The described procedure opens the optional-work view first; this option does not match that reviewed entry point.
optionExplanations.C: The source does not open a separate Case-settings form for the requested optional-work configuration procedure.
optionExplanations.D: User management is an access/people context, not the workflow authoring entry point described for optional work.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO are examples of built-in optional Actions that Pega Platform provides by default?

options.text: Edit details
Change Stage
Cancel Order
Update Contact

practiceQuiz.hint: Pega provides built-in optional Actions — not all are custom-created.
practiceQuiz.rationale: 'Edit details' and 'Change Stage' are built-in optional Actions that Pega Platform provides by default. 'Cancel Order' and 'Update Contact' are examples from the Academy lesson — they are custom optional Actions configured by the SA.

optionExplanations.A: Edit details is a built-in Case-wide example named by the source, rather than a custom contact workflow in its example.
optionExplanations.B: Change Stage is another built-in example and shows why optional does not mean no lifecycle navigation effect.
optionExplanations.C: Cancel Order is the source’s configured business-process example, not an asserted universally built-in action for every Case Type.
optionExplanations.D: Update Contact is an application-specific example, not the source’s named built-in pair requested here.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Request Expedited Review requires three distinct configured Steps with separate workflow progression: capture reason, assign reviewer, confirm. Which optional-work type directly represents the series?

options.text: Optional Process — three Steps are required, so a Process is the right choice
Optional Action — the entire flow is considered one 'request' action
Either — optional Actions can contain multiple Steps through sub-forms
Neither — multi-step user-initiated flows must be implemented as Alternate Stages

practiceQuiz.hint: Multiple Steps = optional Process. Single Step = optional Action.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The described series of separate workflow Steps fits an optional Process. Several fields on one screen would not by themselves create several Steps; the scenario explicitly requires separate progression.

optionExplanations.A: A series of separate workflow Steps directly fits an optional Process rather than merely multiple fields in one view.
optionExplanations.B: Calling the feature one request does not collapse the explicitly separate configured Steps into a single user Action.
optionExplanations.C: Subforms do not change the requirement for separate workflow progression specified here; multiple fields alone would be a different scenario.
optionExplanations.D: The source permits optional Processes for a series; an Alternate Stage is not the only possible design.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which direct lifecycle scope restricts a user-invoked medical-claim Action to Initial Filing, rather than configuring a Case-wide Action with custom applicability logic?

options.text: Add the optional Action as Stage-only, scoped to the 'Initial Filing' Stage
Add the optional Action as Case-wide and add a When Condition to hide it in other Stages
Add the optional Action to each individual Assignment within 'Initial Filing'
Create a Promoted Action for 'Initial Filing' that automatically converts to a standard Action in other Stages

practiceQuiz.hint: An optional Action available only during one specific Stage has Stage-only scope.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Stage-only directly represents the stated lifecycle scope. Custom Case-wide applicability is an alternative design pattern, not proof that scope is unnecessary or that all other configurations are impossible.

optionExplanations.A: Stage-only directly expresses the requested one-Stage lifecycle scope without adding custom Case-wide applicability logic.
optionExplanations.B: The question explicitly requests direct scope rather than this alternate custom applicability pattern; it is not claimed technically impossible.
optionExplanations.C: Repeated Assignment-level association does not identify the lifecycle scope requested for the optional Action.
optionExplanations.D: Promotion changes presentation; it does not automatically switch a task from Stage-only to standard availability elsewhere.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which statement best describes the relationship between optional Actions and the required Case workflow?

options.text: Users can invoke optional work when applicable; the resulting workflow effect depends on the configured Action or Process
Optional Actions temporarily replace required Steps — the Case resumes required Steps after the optional Action completes
Optional Actions are pre-conditions — the required workflow cannot advance until all available optional Actions are invoked
Optional Actions run in parallel with required Processes as separate Case threads

practiceQuiz.hint: Change Stage and cancellation are counterexamples to a universal no-redirection guarantee.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Optional means users may invoke the work in its configured scope. It does not force completing every optional task, nor guarantee no redirect or interruption; Change Stage and cancellation can affect progression.

optionExplanations.A: Optional availability and configured effects are distinct; an invoked Change Stage task can change progression while remaining optional.
optionExplanations.B: Optional work does not universally replace required Steps temporarily; its effect depends on the actual configured task.
optionExplanations.C: Optional work is not a requirement to perform every available menu item before the Case can progress.
optionExplanations.D: The source does not define every optional user Action as a separate parallel Case thread; invocation and structure differ.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is configuring Case-wide optional Actions for a Claims application. Which TWO statements correctly describe Case-wide optional Actions in Pega?

options.text: Case-wide is lifecycle-wide scope rather than restriction to one Stage, subject to applicability and user access
When selected by the reviewed promotion behavior, an eligible Case-wide user Action can appear as a Case summary button
Case-wide optional Actions are only available during the first Stage of a Case and disappear afterward
Case-wide optional Actions automatically create a child Case each time a user triggers them

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate lifecycle scope from promotion eligibility and access permissions.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Case-wide expresses scope. If runtime promotion selects an eligible user Action, it can be shown as a summary button. That is not automatic promotion of every Case-wide Action or an access bypass.

optionExplanations.A: This states lifecycle scope without assuming every user has access or every applicability condition is automatically satisfied.
optionExplanations.B: Eligible user-Action promotion can add a summary button; the source does not say every Case-wide task becomes prominent automatically.
optionExplanations.C: Restriction to the first Stage contradicts Case-wide lifecycle scope; Stage-only is the separate scope choice.
optionExplanations.D: Optional designation does not by itself create child Cases; an invoked task would need configured creation behavior.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer configures a 'Request Additional Documents' optional Action as Stage-only for the Review Stage of a Claims Case. Which TWO behaviors does this optional Action exhibit at runtime?

options.text: The optional Action is only available to users while the Case is in the Review Stage
When the Case exits the Review Stage, the optional Action is no longer visible to users
The optional Action remains available in all Stages indefinitely once it has been triggered once
Stage-only optional Actions automatically reset the Stage SLA timer each time they are triggered

practiceQuiz.hint: Stage-only Actions are visible only while that Stage is active — they disappear when the Case leaves the Stage.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The configured Stage scope determines when the task can be launched through that availability. Invocation does not permanently make it Case-wide. No automatic SLA reset follows merely from being optional; configured Action behavior remains a separate concern.

optionExplanations.A: Stage-only scope limits launching the task in the configured Stage context, subject to actual applicability and access.
optionExplanations.B: Leaving that Stage removes its Stage-only availability; it does not automatically grant lifecycle-wide availability after invocation.
optionExplanations.C: One invocation does not convert the configured scope into permanent Case-wide availability in every later Stage.
optionExplanations.D: No automatic SLA reset follows merely from optional invocation; timer effects would require separate configured behavior.

quickRecap.value: Optional Action = single Step (e.g., 'Update customer info'). Optional Process = series of Steps (e.g., 'Cancel Order'). Both are user-initiated, not required.
Case-wide provides lifecycle scope; Stage-only applies in one Stage context. Applicable configuration and user access still matter.
Actions menu in the Case. Promoted Actions also appear as buttons on the Case Page for higher visibility.
Runtime summary-button promotion supports user Actions, not optional Processes. Inspect the source’s Stage-wide then Case-wide selection behavior.
Workflow tab → 'Optional Actions' button (upper-right corner of Case Life Cycle). No separate Rule form.
The reviewed source names Edit details and Change Stage as built-in Case-wide examples; it does not establish an immutable universal count.
Optional describes user invocation. The invoked task’s configuration determines its effects; Change Stage or cancellation can change progression.
